name: rhl-lines-board
description: Tools for the warehouse lines board (lines A to S, each holding jobs). Same data and same access rule as the human web UI: reads are open, writes need a temporary per-employee key issued by the person's own agent. Names are snake_case and convert directly to MCP tools (name, description, inputSchema), Claude tool definitions (input_schema) and other tool registries.

limits.controlCharacters: not allowed in title, details or initials

access.read: open: needs only the project URL and the public anon key
access.write: needs a board key (ergk_...) on every write call (job_save, job_set_status, job_remove) and on key_check. Keys are temporary (at most 30 days), scoped to this app and issued for a specific employee by that person's own agent. The key is read from configuration (BOARD_KEY), never passed as a tool argument and never echoed back.
access.credentials: There is no passcode and no shared secret. Never ask a human to type or tell you a secret, never use a service-role key, and never put a key in a URL query string. To hand a key to a browser, open the app with the key in the URL fragment (#key=...), which no server or log sees.

attribution: WHO changed a job is authoritative in the read-only `updated_by` field, which the database sets server-side from the subject of the validated key (the employee the key was issued for). It cannot be supplied by a caller: no tool accepts `updated_by`, and a value sent in a payload is rejected or ignored. `initials` is only a display tag: agent writes stamp it with a short actor tag (default AGT, configurable via BOARD_ACTOR, max 6 chars) when `initials` is not passed, and it can say anything. Trust `updated_by`, not `initials`.
testData: Rows with is_test = true are synthetic TEST rows. board_get returns test_data: true when any row is a TEST row. Do not write to a board whose test_data is true unless your user explicitly asked you to test.

errorCodes.key_invalid: The key is unknown, revoked or issued for a different app (one answer for all three). Do not retry; ask your own agent to issue a new key for this employee.
errorCodes.key_expired: The key is known but past its expiry. Do not retry; ask your own agent to issue a new key for this employee.
errorCodes.invalid: The arguments failed validation (checked locally before any network call, and again by the database). Fix the arguments; message names the offending fields.
errorCodes.not_found: No job with that id (for an edit with expected_revision or for job_set_status/job_remove: it is gone, nothing was written and nothing was recreated).
errorCodes.network: The board could not be reached after retries (or an unexpected server reply). Safe to try again later: writes carry a client-generated id so a repeat never duplicates a job.
errorCodes.config: Connection settings are missing or unusable (BOARD_URL, BOARD_ANON_KEY, BOARD_KEY), the key is not an ergk_ key, or the anon key was rejected.
errorCodes.conflict: The job's stored revision differs from expected_revision: someone changed it since you read it. Nothing was written; the result carries current_revision. Do not retry the same call: re-read the job (board_find / board_get), decide whether your change still applies, then call again with the new revision.

tools.name: board_get
tools.description: Read the whole board: all lines A to S in order, each with its jobs (id, title, details, initials, status open/hold/ready/done, revision), plus whether any row is TEST data. Use this first to learn current state, to get job ids, and to check test_data before writing. Do not use it to look for one job by text (use board_find) and do not poll it faster than every few seconds. Each job carries read-only updated_by (who last changed it, from the key subject). No key needed.

test_data.description: true when any line or job on the board is a synthetic TEST row

truncated.description: true if the job list hit the server row cap and is incomplete

updated_by.description: Read-only. The subject of the key that made the last change, set by the database. Null for rows never written through a key.

tools.name: board_find
tools.description: Find jobs by text, line and/or status. Text is a case-insensitive substring match over title, details and initials. Use it to locate a job id before changing it. Do not use it to list the whole board (use board_get). All filters are optional and combined with AND. Each job carries read-only updated_by (who last changed it, from the key subject). No key needed.

text.description: Substring to look for in title, details or initials.

total_matches.description: Matches before the limit was applied

items.description: A job as in board_get plus line_code and line_id.

updated_by.description: Read-only. The subject of the key that made the last change, set by the database. Null for rows never written through a key.

tools.name: job_save
tools.description: Create a job on a line, or update an existing one. Pass `id` (a uuid you generate) to make the call idempotent: repeating it never creates a second job. Omit `id` and the client generates one and returns it; keep it to edit later. When updating, send only the fields you want to change; omitted fields keep their value. A new job needs a title and a line (line_code or line_id). Writes need a board key (BOARD_KEY); if you get key_invalid or key_expired, stop and ask your own agent for a new key. Do not use it just to change status (use job_set_status) and do not write to a board whose test_data is true unless asked. The result's updated_by is set by the database from your key; you cannot set it. To edit safely, pass expected_revision (the `revision` you read): a stale value returns conflict and a deleted job returns not_found, and nothing is written. Creates never take it: a create is an idempotent upsert by id. Omit it only when you deliberately want last-write-wins.

id.description: Job uuid. Optional, client-generated. Same id twice = same job (update).

line_code.description: Line A to S. Required for a new job unless line_id is given; on update, moves the job.

title.description: Customer or job text. Required when creating.

details.description: The note. Empty string clears it.

initials.description: Who touched it. Defaults to the actor tag (AGT).

expected_revision.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard: the job's `revision` as you last read it. If the stored revision differs the write is refused with conflict (nothing changed, current_revision returned); if the job was deleted you get not_found and it is not recreated.

created.description: true if the job did not exist before this call

job.description: The saved row: id, line_id, line_code, title, details, initials, status, revision, is_test, updated_by (read-only, the key's subject), created_at, updated_at.

tools.name: job_set_status
tools.description: Change only the status of an existing job (open, hold, ready, done). Use it for quick moves such as marking a job ready. Do not use it to change anything else (use job_save) or to delete (use job_remove); it cannot create a job. Needs a board key; on key_invalid or key_expired stop and ask your own agent for a new key. It reads the job's current revision and writes with it, so a change by someone else in between returns conflict instead of silently overwriting; pass expected_revision yourself to guard against changes since an earlier read.

expected_revision.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard: the job's `revision` as you last read it. If the stored revision differs the write is refused with conflict (nothing changed, current_revision returned); if the job was deleted you get not_found and it is not recreated.

job.description: The saved row: id, line_id, line_code, title, details, initials, status, revision, is_test, updated_by (read-only, the key's subject), created_at, updated_at.

tools.name: job_remove
tools.description: Permanently delete a job. There is no undo. Use only when your user asked to delete that specific job. Do not use it to finish a job (use job_set_status with done) or to clean up jobs you did not create. Removing an already removed job returns not_found. Needs a board key; on key_invalid or key_expired stop and ask your own agent for a new key.

tools.name: key_check
tools.description: Check that your board key works and see who it was issued for and when it expires. Use it once before a batch of writes, or when a write returned key_invalid or key_expired and you have been given a new key. Do not use it to test other people's keys, and do not loop on it: on key_invalid or key_expired stop and ask your own agent for a new key. Writes nothing.

subject.description: The employee the key was issued for

expires_at.description: ISO timestamp when the key stops working

keys.rule: Keys are 256-bit random (ergk_ plus 43 base64url characters) and stored hashed, so there is no throttle and no lockout. A wrong key is simply key_invalid.
keys.agentRule: Never retry on key_invalid or key_expired. Stop and ask your own agent (or the person's key tool) to issue a new key for this employee. Never invent, guess or reuse another person's key.
